title: Counting with While
story: Your gym teacher says: "Give me 10 jumping jacks and count them out loud!" You start at 1, do a jumping jack, say "one," then move to 2. You keep going until you hit 10. A `while` loop does exactly this � it repeats while counting up!
why: Counting loops are the foundation of automation � they let programs repeat actions an exact number of times for timers, animations, and batch processing.
analogy: A while loop counting up is like climbing stairs � you start at step 1 and keep climbing until you reach the top.
try_it: Print the 5 times table from 1 x 5 to 12 x 5. Then change the step to count by 2s or 3s. What happens if you change `i += 1` to a bigger number?
tips: Always make sure your counter eventually makes the condition false � otherwise your loop runs forever!
Print the counter inside the loop to watch it change � it helps you understand what's happening
Use `io.print()` (without `ln`) to print multiple things on the same line before ending with `io.println()`
common_mistakes: Forgetting to update the counter � `i += 1;` inside the loop is what makes it eventually stop!
Starting the counter at the wrong value � if you want numbers 1 to 10, start at 1 with `<= 10`, not at 0 with `< 10`
